b.statement:
Read concepts and systems through one another to generate interference patterns. Diffraction produces knowledge; reflection reproduces the same.
Art reconfigures the agential cut by introducing a second-order loop where the observer's framing becomes part of the system—a diffractive shift from optimizing a fixed telos to attending to the apparatus that makes that telos intelligible, holding the incompatibility between vector spaces as the generative membrane through which new ontologies emerge. The cut is the minimal unit of observation and world-constitution.

source_excerpts.content:
Your notes extend the volume’s field. They trace a <mark id="note-highlight-ef023abd-13ff-48d8-ae84-9ab9fc900ca9" data-note-id="ef023abd-13ff-48d8-ae84-9ab9fc900ca9">conceptual arc from open systems to closure</mark>, then unsettle that arc with unresolved tensions: <mark id="note-highlight-7633bccc-49cd-4515-94c5-37455911e91a" data-note-id="7633bccc-49cd-4515-94c5-37455911e91a">the paradox of operational closure vs. open exchange</mark>, the status of information, the dialectic of control and emergence. Two threads in particular diffract through our earlier conversation.

First, the question of *how art “corrects” purposive rationality toward wisdom.* The verb *correct* presumes a norm—a rational goal-seeking that requires adjustment. But the volume’s own tensions suggest a more radical possibility: <mark id="note-highlight-ba531869-4a5f-498d-9b97-a5d215e85f30" data-note-id="ba531869-4a5f-498d-9b97-a5d215e85f30">art doesn’t correct rationality so much as </mark>*<mark data-note-id="ba531869-4a5f-498d-9b97-a5d215e85f30">reconfigure the agential cut.</mark>*<mark data-note-id="ba531869-4a5f-498d-9b97-a5d215e85f30"> In cybernetic terms, purposive rationality is a first-order feedback loop: goal, action, measurement of deviation, correction. Art—especially the “aesthetics of behavior” that Penny and the Japanese neocybernetics gesture toward—introduces a second-order loop where the observer’s own framing, desire, and embodiment become part of the system. That isn’t correction; it’s a diffractive shift from optimizing a fixed telos to attending to the apparatus that makes that telos intelligible.</mark> Wisdom, then, is not a destination but the capacity to hold the cut open—to let uncertainty, noise, and the voice of the material substrate participate in the loop.

This connects to your second unresolved thread: reconciling Luhmann’s functional differentiation with ANT’s flat ontology. In the book, Luhmann’s systems seem to cleave along discipline lines (law, science, art) while ANT refuses a priori boundaries. But the book also offers cosmotechnics as a challenge to universalist cybernetics. What if functional differentiation is itself a local cultural cut—a Eurocentric one—rather than a universal structural necessity? ANT’s flat ontology, by contrast, refuses to pre-define what counts as a system, leaving that to the performative associations of actors.
